pr_body:
Motivation:

Provides legacy support for client TCP fast open.

Modification:

Provides TCP fast open for TCP epoll client sockets. This _could_ normally be available via the TCP_FASTOPEN_CONNECT epoll option, but this isn't supported on older kernels (only 4.11+). This newer option is mostly a convenience feature for the original functionality described [here](https://lwn.net/Articles/508865/), so I have provided an implementation that uses the original functionality to extend support to linux kernel 3.6+.

Result:

Fixes #9651.

Notes:

This replaces the existing functionality for TCP_FASTOPEN_CONNECT. This implementation should be functionally similar while providing support for legacy kernels. The new implementation is included in the epoll test permutations, but is excluded from some tests. This is to be expected given that client fast open effectively makes the first phase of the connection stateless, and will alter some expected behavior you would normally have with TCP connections that have a stateful connect phase. 

The existing TCP_FASTOPEN_CONNECT option was not present in any tests or the epoll permutations so it is unknown whether it would have the same effect on the tests, but it is assumed so.

- [ ] Squashed
- [X] Public API compatibility
- [X] Feature parity
- [X] Epoll test permutations (with some exceptions)
- [x] EpollSocketFileRegionTest behavior confirmation
- [x] Review of test case exceptions


Caveat/oddity signoff:
- [ ] No support for sendFile
- [ ] Replaces existing TCP_FASTOPEN_CONNECT mechanics (at parity but more broad kernel support)
- [ ] Elevated doWriteOrSendBytes to AbstractEpollChannel.java 
- [ ] Changes to access levels on some methods

Hey @colinrgodsey is this still something you're interested in working on? I did a rebase locally, and the conflicts weren't hard to resolve.

I have questions about the approach taken here, though. You've made the fast-open work by delaying the actual connecting until the first write. I think it would be better if people instead had to queue up a write prior to connecting, so that to use fast-open you'd have to write something like this:

```
boostrap.register().sync().channel().write(...);
boostrap.connect(...);
```

Doing things that way means the error handling around `connect()` should work like it usually does, and also it's more explicit that a write is being queued up. I think that makes sense because the processing of the data delivered with the SYN packet needs to be idempotent on the server side, and requiring the write before the connect makes it something you have to go out of your way to opt into.

issue_context.title: Add proper support for TCP Fast Open in native transport
issue_context.body:
We currently support to set the TCP_FAST_OPEN `ChannelOption` in our native epoll transport.  While this is generally good enough for servers it is not good enough for client-side usage. Here we will need to introduce the usage of `sendto(...)` to replace the usage of `connect(...)` when TCP_FAST_OPEN is used.

See https://lwn.net/Articles/508865/
comments: Going to take a crack at this today

I'm guessing we'll have to let the channel connect 'optimistically' succeed until data is first sent. Kind of necessary to allow the '0RTT' transmission there. 

EDIT: TCP_FASTOPEN_CONNECT preserves the same connect/send usage, but it seems pretty new (2017): https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/commit/?id=19f6d3f3c8422d65b5e3d2162e30ef07c6e21ea2 That support seems to already be in Netty, so going to assume this is just for the original FASTOPEN style

Now I'm getting all hung up trying to figure out how to handle TCP_FASTOPEN_CONNECT vs TCP_FASTOPEN... there doesn't seem to be any way to test for TCP_FASTOPEN_CONNECT support. I wonder if its worth just replacing the TCP_FASTOPEN_CONNECT functionality with the classic TCP_FASTOPEN? The _CONNECT form seems to just be boilerplate to make workflow with TCP_FASTOPEN easier. Netty users will be blind to the underlying implementation anyways (also, the TCP_FASTOPEN channel option is an Integer types which makes it kind of odd with the client implementation, as there's no threshold).

EDIT: this would also avoid introducing any additional API changes

I've got this so far: https://github.com/netty/netty/compare/4.1...colinrgodsey:4.1_fastopen

Code format clobbered some random things, so need to fix that... plus some other cleanup, and some new tests.

(sorry, just journaling things here...)

Yea, I really think hijacking TCP_FASTOPEN_CONNECT is the best option. There's not actually a socket flag for client fast open anyways, its just a special flag on "sendto". While it's kind of a "lie" that we're not actually using the new TCP_FASTOPEN_CONNECT flag, we are effectively doing the same thing (from what I can tell in the kernel code, the end effects are reasonably identical). So this extends existing functionality without introducing any visible API changes.
~Works now, getting through tests.... seems to be some weirdness with LEVEL_TRIGGERED epoll, and one of the connect tests (doesnt like the empty local address)~

Alright, so I added client fast open to the epoll permutations and.... lots of things are failing. The normal data transmission pattern stuff works, so thats good (overall write pattern works), but it seems to failing with ~some of the epoll trigger mechanics and~ the connection mechanics. not surprising about the connection mechanics, this does ultimately change how all of that works. still working through the tests

EDIT: I might have to take the fast connection client out of the permutations... many edge cases so far :(

Alright, so... some things to consider:

a) Should TCP_FASTOPEN_CONNECT be replaced with the more-compatible sendto/sendmsg form.
b) TCP_FASTOPEN_CONNECT doesn't seem to have been in any tests, and it likely exhibits the same behavior issues as the other form, but not sure. 
c) Should the behavior changes be considered "expected", and a normal caveat of the feature? (it is after all a stateless connection). These caveats can be handled piecemeal in the Epoll test suite to help further cement which behaviors are expected to be violated. 

Personally, I think it's best to leave the fastopen behavior in the epoll permutations, and for each test case that is violated by the fastopen behavior, provide a different EpollSocketTestPermutation that leaves out the fastopen client. That way its searchable and can be used as a definitive source for producing a list of 'caveats' for TCP client fastopen.

yeah, the actual (untouched) `doConnect()` method will check if a remoteAddress is already set and fail before `doConnect0()` (which has an override here) is called, so the AlreadyConnectedException will still be thrown using the expected behavior (it doesnt rely on the actual socket state).
